name: Equal tangent segments
formula: PA = PB \text{ for tangents from } P, \qquad \text{incircle: tangent length from } A = s - a
whenToUse: Two tangent lines are drawn to a circle from one point, or a circle is inscribed in a triangle or quadrilateral and side lengths are involved.
example: In a triangle with $BC = 14$, $CA = 15$, $AB = 13$, we have $s = 21$, so the incircle touches the sides at distances $21 - 14 = 7$ from $A$, $21 - 15 = 6$ from $B$ and $21 - 13 = 8$ from $C$. Check: $7 + 6 = 13$.
pitfall: The tangent length from vertex $A$ is $s$ minus the side OPPOSITE $A$. A quadrilateral with an incircle has equal sums of opposite sides.
derivation: The two right triangles formed by $P$, the center and each tangent point share a hypotenuse and have equal legs (radii), so they are congruent.
